chapter: Louis Armstrong, King Oliver and St. Louis memories
title: The Chauffeurs' Club and bouncer Joe Giggles
summary: Thomas returns to hearing Armstrong at the Chauffeurs' Club after the Paradise, and describes bouncer and prizefighter Joe Giggles.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Well, tell me, well, of course, you could just merely chat with Joe Oliver at this time.

I didn't have a chance to chat with him. I tell you what I guess it must be in your raising. Back to Pops, Louis Armstrong ... so I heard him. He did this tune. It was on a Sunday afternoon, no Sunday night. He played the afternoon at a little place called the Paradise so he comes back that Sunday night and plays at Chauffer's Club. You know St. Louis is a big musical town.
What was the name of this club?
The Chauffer's Club. Joe Giggles. You don't know Joe Giggles. Joe Giggles was a bouncer. He was a prize fighter.
Joe Giggles, Joe Grant. I was the only one in New York that called him Joe Giggles. ...
Did he run the Chauffer's Club?
No, he's a bouncer. And the guy didn't look like he should come in, he couldn't come in. He's also the bouncer at the Booker T. Washington.
This is really where you got to hear Louis, was it?

Stanley and Baby, I told Baby about this many times. So I told Pops about it, we talked one day and I think I had gone to see him with Don Redman. We were going to hear Louis at the Paramount. So we get to talking and they got to talking about something so I didn't bother ... so one day I had a little gig. I was at the Paramount in the basement of the Paramount, you know at the Chiles. And we had some things going there so I told him about this. So he played a tune. So, Joe Giggles was said, Let me in. He could pass. May I say The man said thanks. I always got to say thanks.
